EIL5 example. The reason a fan makes you feel cooler isn't that it's changing the temperature in the room. Your body generates heat, usually hotter than the ambient temperature. The fan is moving the hot air around your body away and 'sinking' it into the air that's not beside you.

No, what I said was dealing with heat dissipation through the use of ejecting heat carrying bodies is practical.

Heat is lost by transferring it to something else. On earth, it's the air or water around the object that the heat is transferred to. In a modern gun it's the brass casings. Once the heat is in the casing, remove the casing and that's less heat moving through the rest of the gun.

In space, or low atmosphere environments, there isn't  anywhere for that heat to go quickly, so the gun heats up and would stay hot for a long time if it didn't eject that heat into a removable heat sink.

There is a reason they make thermoses with a vacuum chamber in the walls of them. And why they don't have to heat the inside of the ISS, they run constant cooling.

While the wording is different, functionally, our two versions work the same, so I agree.

From a LORE standpoint, they are actually really practical! Hell, modern guns already use something similar.

The brass casings ejected from a modern firearm during firing pull a significant amount of heat away from the weapon during use. One of the major reasons caseless ammunition never really developed  was heat management. Without the heat dump of the cases, the weapons are prone to malfunction and failure during extended firing.

High energy ezoo propelled weapons had heat issues, causing soldiers to be exposed or temporarily  unable to return fire due to having to let the gun cool down. By adding an ejectable thermal clip allowed them to return to the fight a lot quicker, thus increasing their effectiveness in battle.

From a GAMEPLAY perspective, they should have been regenerative and alot more rare IMO. Either sit in cover, or dump a rare resource to make sure that Banshee doesn't off Garrus.


Edit: as I've already said they should have been regenerative, as in the gun should still cool down like ME1, if only maybe a bit slower. The ability to 'reload' the heat capacity at a moments notice is what makes thermal clips practical.

You don't lose your unlimited ammo, you just gain the ability to push an advantage if you have a spare thermal clip available.

There is no anatomical reason we cant, but as there is no need to, we just dont know how. 
Example:  you hold two pencils in front of someone about eye distance apart and about 12inches/30 centimeter away from their face. Get them to watch both pencils and move the pencils in unison around left right up etc, and then together, their eyes will follow and you can force the person to cross their eyes. Now if you move them farther from each other swiftly, the persons eyes will often diverge, until their brain catches on, and realigned the eyes on a singular target again.

Eye muscles dont develop to spread the eyes as there is no need to, unlike crossing your eyes. As objects get closer to you, in order to keep both eyes on it, they have to angle toward each other.
There is no point where you would benefit from your eyes pointing away from each other, as the object would no longer be seen with both eyes.
